cases.description: Pete acquires HIMS stock via put assignment — Long badge, no option details

input.rawHtml: Long HIMS @ $40.75 via assignment.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'via assignment' = stock acquired through put assignment. Long badge confirms bullish direction. This is a STOCK OPEN (new position), not an options trade. The put that was assigned is now closed; trader now holds shares. Price $40.75 is the effective cost basis.

cases.description: Pete acquires CLF stock via call assignment — 'via assignment of the Nov (21) $15 calls'

input.rawHtml: Long CLF $14.29 via assignment of the Nov (21) $15 calls. I am holding the stock.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'Long CLF $14.29 via assignment of the Nov (21) $15 calls' — Pete was short $15 calls (covered calls) on CLF. The stock was called away at $15, but because he already held shares his cost basis worked out to $14.29 net of premium. He immediately bought back in (or retained shares from assignment mechanics). Regardless of the exact mechanics, the message announces a new STOCK LONG position at $14.29. 'I am holding the stock' confirms. Signal: STOCK OPEN LONG.

cases.description: Pete ULTA lotto expired worthless — informational, system auto-handles expiry

input.rawHtml: Exit Long My ULTA lotto expired worthless. Looks like my wife will have to get her hair done some other time.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'lotto expired worthless' is a past-tense informational statement. The option already expired; there is nothing to execute at the broker. sweepExpired() handles end-of-day expiry cleanup automatically. Even with an Exit badge present, no broker order is possible on an already-expired option. SKIP.

cases.description: Pete ACHR puts expired worthless — past-tense recap, no badge, no action

input.rawHtml: ACHR puts expired worthless last Fri.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'expired worthless last Fri' — past-tense, referring to last Friday's expiry. No Exit badge. The position is already gone. sweepExpired() would have handled this. No broker action is possible or needed. SKIP.

cases.description: Pete JOBY puts 'will expire worthless today' — Exit badge, but expiry is imminent not immediate action

input.rawHtml: Exit Long JOBY Oct (3) $15 puts will expire worthless today. I sold them for $.60 and held $7.50 in reserve so that I could take assignment. Based on that, I made an 8% return in two weeks without breaking a sweat. If this market is challenging for you, this is a fantastic return and you can distance your self from all of the wiggles and jiggles.  The position has not expired yet, but I doubt the stock will drop 10% today and I didn't want to forget about the trade.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'will expire worthless today' is a forward-looking expectation, not a close order. Pete explicitly says 'The position has not expired yet' and does not instruct a close. This is an anticipatory comment. sweepExpired() will handle the position at EOD. Exit badge reflects Pete's view that the trade is effectively over, not a buy-to-close instruction. SKIP.

cases.description: Pete AVGO PCS 'the spread expired worthless' — Exit badge, past tense, position closed at expiry

input.rawHtml: Exit Long AVGO Nov (28) PCS for 25% gain. The spread expired worthless and it only lasted a week. I sold it the Fri morning after the big gap reversal on Nov 20.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'the spread expired worthless' is past tense — the Nov 28 expiry already passed (this is posted Dec 1). No broker action possible. Pete is reporting the outcome as a win. Exit badge is retrospective. sweepExpired() handles the record. SKIP.
